scanScope: Garnier 1877 pp. 105–107, continuing on the first prose lines of p. 108 until CHAPITRE II; all seven chapter I paragraphs and headings compared visually

canonicalCorrection.reason: Preserve printed two-word orthography; the same online normalization also occurs in chapter II on p. 108 and is logged in the dossier.

sourceDecisions: Selected the 1877 printed body. Keep the chapter title and summary as navigation metadata, not editorial note text.
Keep géomètres in the literary body on p. 105; algébristes is only an alternative reported in the historical footnote.
Do not import any numbered editor footnote or the typographic running heads into learner prose.
Keep the chapter's historical spellings, e.g. muphti, and its original measurements; do not modernize quantities or silently change the satire.

unitReview.decision: 29 thought units reconstruct five paragraphs; eight passages have 104–139 word tokens, complete original order and no single-sentence passage.
manualBoundaries: Divide the very long geometrical sentence after the original semicolon before « ils trouveront, dis-je » so the result can be read in two connected units.
Keep the narrator's « Ce n’est pas ... ! mais Micromégas ... » aside together as one thought unit.

contextNotes: The plural microscopes has one metaphorical use for the giants' eyes; the same optical-instrument meaning remains clear in context.
The secretary denotes a Saturnian academy official and later the Paris Academy official; it never denotes furniture.
Toises are historical lengths with no universal conversion asserted; berline denotes a horse-drawn coach, not a modern sedan.
Questions at Levels 4–5 use same-number and same-gender noun alternatives; actual meaning must resolve the blank.
The singular habitant and plural habitants have the same lexical sense but require separate surface-plus-sense mastery identities.
The giants liken humans to insectes; the metaphor shares the insect referent, while distinct literal uses also occur.
The noun êtres is kept apart from finite forms of être; physical smallness is kept apart from a character judgment.
The expression de planète en planète and the compound compagnon de voyage remain on the expression review list.
Level 4–5 noun choices were manually checked for agreement with each sentence and a single semantic answer.
Euclid's mathematical propositions are separated from the two later uses meaning controversial doctrinal assertions.
The numerical forms cinquante and huit have stable values across historical measures, ages and counts.
Tiers is one third, fraction is a part of a whole, and citoyens is used rhetorically for members of a planet's community.
All ten forms have exact workwide spans; the final meaning, shared sense and question reviews remain pending.
The hyphenated sur-le-champ is reviewed as one vocabulary token, following expression review 01.
Lois means physical principles here, rayon is sunlight, and forces are physical attraction/repulsion; other lemma senses must remain distinct.
Attractives and répulsives agree with feminine plural forces; each Level 4–5 blank has four grammatically compatible choices.
Académie refers to both Saturn's and Paris's scholarly institutions; lier conversation remains a collocation for later expression review.
Disséqua describes anatomical dissection, while se dérobent aux microscopes means escaping observation, not theft or deliberate concealment.
Vétillard denotes nitpicking; malsonnantes and téméraires are historically specific theological censure labels, checked against period dictionary entries.
Suspectes and hérétiques are the mufti’s accusations, not authorial confirmation of the book’s supposed error.
Puces and colimaçons are animals in the mufti’s fanciful dispute; condamner applies to the book, distinct from sentencing its author.
Plural noun blanks use alternatives matching the target’s number and gender; final question approval remains pending.

decisions: à peu près reuses the existing published à plus locution sense identity and three-band vocabulary quiz; preserve the old mastery identity and do not introduce independent expression mastery.
se mettre à maps past mit to its published identity and present met to a new surface under the existing reflexive-begin sense; keep separate surface mastery and no independent expression item.
sur-le-champ is a single hyphenated lexical token; route it to vocabulary rather than a separate expression.
de même nature and the repeated-noun de X en X constructions are compositional here; ne … que is a productive grammatical restriction.
Temporal au bout de is distinguished from the spatial tip of a telescope; only the temporal reading has an expression question draft.

abbreviations: Printed M. denotes Monsieur. The tokenizer indexes M and leaves the period in prose; reuse the published M surface under the monsieur lemma and title sense, preserving its existing mastery and three question bands.
additionalTriage.note: Lists are triage, not exhaustive coverage. All other chapter tokens and expression spans still require contextual decisions.

remaining: Resolve 82 unassigned chapter I tokenizer uses, including historical senses, expressions, and inflections. Twenty-four named-entity uses have explicit vocabulary exclusions while remaining in the literary text.
Review shared published senses and all three prepared quiz bands before approving any chapter or complete-work learner bundle.
Only import after all seven chapters, chapter headings and per-work publication checks are complete.

contextNotes: The latest journey is dernier, not the published Zola latter sense; au public is people in general, not the existing accessible adjective.
The narrator’s dis-je is first-person speech; useful geometers and ordinary calculations are satirical statements without changing the basic lexical senses.
All ten forms occur exactly once in this work; published sense reuse and all question bands still need final editorial approval.
États are political territories; souverains are their rulers; empire supplies the scale comparison. None of these words is approved solely from orthography.
Comparés indicates side-by-side consideration; image is a weak representation, and prodigieuses refers to astonishingly large differences, not literal magic.
Ceinture is a belt, septième is the ordinal of the facial proportion, démontrer closes an ironical proof, and coutume is a social practice. All ten forms occur once in the work.
Six Level 4–5 noun blanks have four alternatives with the required number and gender; semantic and shared-sense signoff remain pending.
